name: Girdle-tracking shoulder
about: The tilted gimbal rides on a passive two-joint link on the back that lets its centre move up, down, forward and back with the real shoulder joint. A spring carries the link's weight. Misalignment is only what it takes to drag the passive joints along.
design_note: First axis, J2 side and motor ring radius picked by a design search over the shoulder range sweep (2026-10-08): the side keeps the middle motor outside the head and neck, and both gimbal-lock directions sit just outside the human range (up and slightly behind overhead, and into the chest). J1 and J3 turn up to 270 degrees each way through a cable wrap. J3 (arm twist) uses the fast, backdrivable quasi-direct drive: the twist needs speed more than torque, and near gimbal lock it spins fastest.
